guide.p: Technology appears in every section of IELTS: questions about smartphones in Part 1, apps in Part 2, automation and privacy in Part 3 and Task 2. These words help you discuss both benefits and risks.

bullets: Learn words in phrases, not alone: notice which verbs, adjectives and prepositions go with them.
Practise each word in a sentence about your own life or country — it will be easier to use in Speaking.
In Writing, choose the precise word over the impressive-sounding one. Accuracy beats complexity.

guide.tip: 'Technology' is usually uncountable in general statements ('Technology has changed our lives'), but 'technologies' is used for specific types ('new medical technologies').

vocab.meaning: the most advanced, newest
vocab.example: The hospital uses cutting-edge scanning equipment.

vocab.meaning: a new idea, method or invention
vocab.example: Innovation is essential for economic growth.

vocab.meaning: an important discovery or development
vocab.example: Scientists made a breakthrough in battery design.

vocab.meaning: computer systems that perform tasks normally needing human intelligence
vocab.example: Artificial intelligence is used to detect fraud.

vocab.meaning: using machines or computers to do work instead of people
vocab.example: Automation has replaced many factory jobs.

vocab.meaning: a set of rules a computer follows to solve a problem
vocab.example: Social media algorithms decide what we see.

vocab.meaning: a piece of electronic equipment
vocab.example: Most teenagers own more than one device.

vocab.meaning: easy to use
vocab.example: The app is user-friendly, even for older people.

vocab.meaning: good at using modern technology
vocab.example: Younger employees are often more tech-savvy.

vocab.meaning: no longer used because something newer exists
vocab.example: Fax machines are now almost obsolete.

vocab.meaning: to improve a device or system to a newer version
vocab.example: The company upgrades its laptops every three years.

vocab.meaning: the ability to use digital technology effectively
vocab.example: Digital literacy should be taught in schools.

vocab.meaning: the gap between people who have access to technology and those who do not
vocab.example: The digital divide leaves rural families at a disadvantage.

vocab.meaning: protection of personal information
vocab.example: Users are increasingly worried about data privacy.

vocab.meaning: protection of computer systems from attack
vocab.example: Banks spend heavily on cybersecurity.

vocab.meaning: bullying that takes place online
vocab.example: Schools are tackling cyberbullying through education.

vocab.meaning: time spent looking at screens
vocab.example: Doctors recommend limiting children's screen time.

vocab.meaning: buying and selling goods online
vocab.example: E-commerce has forced many high-street shops to close.

vocab.meaning: done from a distance, e.g. working from home
vocab.example: Remote working became common after 2020.

vocab.meaning: existing online or through a computer rather than physically
vocab.example: Students attended virtual classes during the closure.

vocab.meaning: to fail to work properly
vocab.example: The ticket machines malfunctioned during the storm.

vocab.meaning: to depend on
vocab.example: We rely on our phones for almost everything.

vocab.meaning: making people want to keep doing something
vocab.example: Many games are designed to be addictive.

vocab.meaning: the ability to use or get something
vocab.example: Everyone should have access to fast internet.
